Figure caption: General two-step synthetic protocol to silyl ether ionizable lipids with specific structures of the compounds studied for this report.

Figure caption: In vivo assessment of GVS-18-B6 and literature referenced ionizable lipids for IV delivery. Mice were injected IV with 0.5 mg/kg of EGFP mRNA LNP. (A) Quantification of EGFP protein levels in liver at 24 h postdose by ELISA. (B) MCP-1 levels in plasma at 6 h postdose by ELISA. (C) Lipid levels in liver at multiple time points up to 24 h postdose by LC-MS. N = 3 BALB/c mice per group. Error bars are SEM.

Figure caption: Dose response study in mice to assess tolerability. Mice were injected IV with 1, 2, 4, or 6 mg/kg siRNA LNP containing the specified ionizable lipids. IDEXX analysis of serum ALT (A) or AST levels (B) at 24 h postdose. Plasma MCP-1 (C) or IL-6 (D) measured at 6 h postdose by ELISA. (E) Body weight measured at 24 h postdose and expressed at % relative to predose body weight. N = 4 BALB/c mice per group. ***Animals moribund; early termination prior to 24 h postdose.

Figure caption: Endosomal escape of ionizable lipids formulated with hOTC mRNA. HeLa cells were transfected with human ornithine transcarbamylase (hOTC) mRNA LNP containing various ionizable lipids, including Moderna Lipid 5 (top panel), MC3 (middle panel), and GVS-18-B6 (bottom panel), for 2 h. Samples were fixed, permeabilized and stained using antibodies against endosome markers EEA1 and LAMP1 (green), followed by hOTC (red) and GAPDH (magenta) mRNA FISH. Cell nuclei were then counterstained with DAPI (blue). Arrows indicate colocalization of endosome and hOTC mRNA.

Figure caption: Single dose and repeat dose administrations of GVS-18-B6 LNP in NHP. (A–C) NHP received a single dose of 1 mg/kg hOTC mRNA-LNP via a 60 min IV infusion. Liver and spleen samples (A) were collected at 24 h postdose and analyzed for hOTC protein expression by LC-MS. GVS-18-B6 ionizable lipid levels to assess plasma PK (B) or lipid clearance from NHP liver (C) were measured by LC-MS at the specified time points. (D) NHP received 0.25 mg/kg hEPO mRNA-LNP once every 7 days for a total of 5 doses. Plasma hEPO levels measured by ELISA at the specified time points. (E) Hydrolysis of GVS-18-B6 into M456 and (F) M456 clearance from NHP liver at the specified time points, as determined by LC-MS. N = 3–4 cynomolgus monkeys per group. Error bars are SEM.

Figure caption: Physicochemical characterization of wet and frozen mRNA-LNPs. Analytical testing of mRNA-LNPs stored as wet formulation or post-thawing of frozen mRNA-LNPs stored at −80 °C. Wet LNPs were stored at room temperature (RT) for 0, 1, 3, or 6 months. Wet LNPs and frozen LNPs were stored at 2–8 °C or −80 °C, respectively for 0, 1, 3, 6, or 12 months. (A) Particle size (indicated as solid circles) and polydispersity (indicated as open circles) were measured by DLS. (B) mRNA encapsulation efficiency and (C) mRNA concentration were determined by RiboGreen assay and (D) mRNA integrity was assessed by capillary electrophoresis. (E) GVS-18-B6 concentration and (F) GVS-18-B6 lipid molar ratio were measured by UHPLC.

Figure caption: Physicochemical characterization of frozen mRNA-LNPs upon repeated freeze–thaw cycles. Analytical testing of frozen LNPs stored at −80 °C and thawed to room temperature after 1 to 5 cycles. (A) Particle size and (B) polydispersity were measured by DLS. (C) mRNA encapsulation efficiency and (D) mRNA concentration were determined by RiboGreen assay and (E) mRNA integrity was assessed by capillary electrophoresis. (F) GVS-18-B6 concentration and (G) GVS-18-B6 lipid molar ratio were measured by UHPLC. (H) Mice were injected IV with 0.5 mg/kg EGFP mRNA LNP. Quantification of EGFP protein levels in liver at 24 h postdose by ELISA. N = 4 BALB/c mice per group. Error bars are SEM.

Table caption: Formulation Characteristics and Biological Profiling of Silyl Ether Based Ionizable Lipids
